title: Paycheck Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Take-home pay after federal, FICA and state tax — per paycheque and per year. Enter your gross pay per period, pay frequency, filing status, state, custom state tax rate, pre-tax deductions per period (401(k), health insurance) and extra withholding per period and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A paycheck calculator estimates your take-home pay: gross pay minus federal income tax, Social Security and Medicare (FICA), and state tax. Federal tax is estimated from the 2025 brackets on your taxable income — gross pay less pre-tax deductions and the standard deduction. State tax is estimated at your state's 2025 top rate, so your real state tax is usually lower. Treat every figure as an estimate. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Paycheck Calculator

Start by entering your gross pay per period, then choosing your pay frequency from the list, choosing your filing status from the list, choosing your state from the list, entering your custom state tax rate (%), entering your pre-tax deductions per period (401(k), health insurance) and finally entering your extra withholding per period. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your gross pay for one pay period — the amount before any tax or deductions.
2. Choose your pay frequency: weekly, biweekly, semimonthly or monthly.
3. Pick your filing status and state — state tax is estimated at the top rate, or enter your own with 'Other / custom rate'.
4. Add pre-tax deductions and any extra withholding, then check your net pay.

## Formula

Annual gross = pay per period × periods per year. Taxable income = annual gross − pre-tax deductions − standard deduction (single $15,750; married $31,500; head of household $23,625 for 2025). Federal tax uses the 2025 brackets. Net per period = gross − federal − Social Security − Medicare − state tax − pre-tax deductions − extra withholding.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A $2,500 biweekly paycheque in California, single, with no pre-tax deductions: $65,000 a year, $49,250 taxable after the $15,750 standard deduction, federal tax $5,749 a year ($221.12 per period), Social Security $155.00, Medicare $36.25 and state tax $332.50 — leaving $1,755.13 per paycheque, or $45,633.50 a year. Try the same figures in the [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Gross pay per period: 2500, Pay frequency: Biweekly — every 2 weeks (26), Filing status: Single, State: California — 13.3% top rate, Custom state tax rate: 0 %, Pre-tax deductions per period (401(k), health insurance): 0, Extra withholding per period: 0), the [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) returns Net pay per period: 1,755.13, Federal income tax (estimate): 221.12, Social Security (6.2%): 155, Medicare (1.45%): 36.25, State tax (estimate): 332.5, Annual net pay: 45,633.5, Annual gross pay: 65,000. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## How federal withholding is estimated

Your employer withholds federal tax using IRS tables and your W-4, which reflect your W-4 choices. This calculator annualises your pay, subtracts pre-tax deductions and the standard deduction, applies the 2025 brackets, and divides the result back across your pay periods. The total is usually close for straightforward situations, but it will differ with multiple jobs, bonuses, or itemised deductions.

## What FICA covers

FICA funds Social Security and Medicare. Social Security is 6.2% of wages up to $176,100 for 2025. Medicare is 1.45% of all wages, plus 0.9% over $200,000 ($250,000 married filing jointly). The standard deduction does not reduce FICA, but pre-tax 401(k) contributions do reduce the wages it applies to.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- A higher bracket only taxes the income above the threshold at that rate — your whole pay is never taxed at the top rate.
- Pre-tax 401(k) contributions lower your taxable income and FICA wages, so they cut your tax bill as well as your take-home pay.
- If you get a large refund every year, you are over-withholding; adjust your W-4 to keep more of each paycheque.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why is my actual paycheque different from this estimate?

Real withholding uses IRS tables and your W-4, which account for dependents, multiple jobs and other adjustments this calculator cannot see. State tax is also estimated here at the top rate, while real state tax is usually calculated in brackets. Use the result as a close estimate, not a promise.

### Does this include 401(k) and health insurance?

Yes — enter them as pre-tax deductions per period. They reduce your taxable income and the wages subject to Social Security and Medicare, so they lower your tax as well as your take-home pay. Try it with your own numbers in the [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the additional Medicare tax?

An extra 0.9% on wages over $200,000 ($250,000 married filing jointly), applied only above the threshold. Your employer withholds it automatically once you pass it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Paycheck Calculator](/paycheck-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Paycheck Calculator use?

Annual gross = pay per period × periods per year. Taxable income = annual gross − pre-tax deductions − standard deduction (single $15,750; married $31,500; head of household $23,625 for 2025). Federal tax uses the 2025 brackets. Net per period = gross − federal − Social Security − Medicare − state tax − pre-tax deductions − extra withholding.

### What do I need to use the Paycheck Calculator?

Just Gross pay per period, Pay frequency, Filing status, State, Custom state tax rate, Pre-tax deductions per period (401(k), health insurance) and Extra withholding per period. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
